mentions.name: Open-source Chessbase replacement (chess analytics tool)
mentions.description: A free and open source, cross-platform chess analytics tool positioned as a Chessbase replacement. It uses DuckDB with LLM-generated queries over preprocessed game PGNs and piece hashes to answer natural language questions like head-to-head scores, top US juniors, or games featuring specific openings and sacrifices, and can import a user's Chess.com and Lichess games for similar analysis. It was also used to generate an Adult Chess improvers FIDE rank list across world federations.
mentions.problem: Chessbase can be intimidating for a casual Chess.com beginner looking to go into serious chess prep, so the tool aims to lower the barrier of entry to chess improvement tools.
mentions.audience: Casual Chess.com beginners moving into serious chess preparation and improvement who find Chessbase intimidating
mentions.source_excerpt: I am working on a chess analytics tool, specifically a free and open source replacement of Chessbase in this age of LLMs that can run on all platforms. The idea is to lower the barrier of entry to use a chess improvement tool since Chessbase can be intimidating for a causal Chess.com beginner looking to go into serious chess prep.
